title: CXMT pushes into HBM3E production despite low manufacturing yields
dek: Reported yields highlight why domestic memory substitution is a packaging and manufacturing problem, not just a design announcement.
evidence: Reuters citing people familiar with production; figures not independently audited
takeaway: Forecast accelerator availability from known-good stacked memory and packaging throughput, not nominal production starts.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: Accelerators need high-bandwidth stacked memory; usable stack yield and advanced packaging constrain production more than nominal chip design.

paragraphs: HBM is a throughput bottleneck: Accelerators need high-bandwidth stacked memory; usable stack yield and advanced packaging constrain production more than nominal chip design.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Reuters sources say CXMT intends limited production within two months despite preliminary yields of 20–30%, compared with about 70% cited for SK Hynix.
Test samples reportedly perform closer to prior-generation HBM3 than leading HBM3E offerings.

paragraphs: Early HBM3E production: Reuters sources say CXMT intends limited production within two months despite preliminary yields of 20–30%, compared with about 70% cited for SK Hynix.
Performance lag: Test samples reportedly perform closer to prior-generation HBM3 than leading HBM3E offerings.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: These yields are reporting from people familiar with the process, not audited factory data or a matched manufacturing-cost comparison.
At unchanged input volume, 25% versus 70% yield produces only ~36% as many usable units. Actual stacked-device throughput also depends on packaging and test yield.

paragraphs: Anonymous-source estimates: These yields are reporting from people familiar with the process, not audited factory data or a matched manufacturing-cost comparison.
Yield math: At unchanged input volume, 25% versus 70% yield produces only ~36% as many usable units. Actual stacked-device throughput also depends on packaging and test yield.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: A fab announcing HBM3E production does not mean equivalent volumes of qualifying accelerator memory.
Forecast deployable accelerators using known-good stacks, bandwidth, qualification lead times and packaging capacity—not only nameplate wafer output.

paragraphs: Starts are not shipments: A fab announcing HBM3E production does not mean equivalent volumes of qualifying accelerator memory.
